blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse in the Logistics & Supply Chain context — regulation-first design, a fixed delivery rhythm, and outcomes your board can audit.

In Logistics & Supply Chain, data, analytics & lakehouse is the substrate tower: pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture on databricks and snowflake, streaming and event-driven decisioning, executive bi, master data and cataloging, predictive analytics, and data products that generate revenue. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: data engineering & pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture & migration, real-time streaming & event-driven decisioning — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Carrier portals, EDI and telematics produce a patchwork; the control tower reads yesterday. Exceptions surface as customer complaints.
Planners re-plan routes and loads by hand when trucks break down or orders change; exception queues eat capacity that should improve the network.
Trailer/container/yard assets lack sensing; detention, dwell and theft are discovered in invoices. Cold-chain excursions surface at claim time.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

Delivery composes 7 services from the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower — Data Engineering & Pipeline Modernization, Lakehouse Architecture & Migration, Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning, Enterprise BI & Executive Analytics as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method, with EUDR obligations shaping the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Resilient, observable pipelines: trusted data from source to decision at SLA.
Lakehouse the right way: Unity Catalog governance, cost-aware design and AI-ready foundations.
Decisions at event speed: sub-second pipelines from sensor, click or transaction to action.
Metrics into management: one governed semantic layer, decision cadence built in.
TMS/WMS/telematics/carrier events streamed into one governed estate (network truth in seconds)
Lane-level scope 3 transport emissions with methodology lineage (CSRD-grade reporting automated)
Intercepted in transit, not at claims

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: EUDR and EUDR. Deforestation due diligence for in-scope commodities with evidence duties. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Delivery runs on one weekly rhythm for every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 belong to measurement: the baseline metric is captured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 run a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — steered by a control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 convert the pilot into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, and close with a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses a gate is stopped or redirected on the record.
